{{short description|Concept in statistics}}
{{About|the concept in statistics|other uses|Rake (disambiguation){{!}}Rake}}
'''Raking''' (also called "raking ratio estimation" or "[[iterative proportional fitting]]") is the statistical process of adjusting data sample weights of a contingency table to match desired marginal totals.<ref name="pew">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pewresearch.org/methods/2018/01/26/how-different-weighting-methods-work/|title=1. How different weighting methods work|date=26 January 2018}}</ref><ref name="kalton">{{cite journal |last1=Kalton|first1=Graham|last2=Flores-Cervantes|first2=Ismael|date=2003|title=Weighting Methods|url=https://www.scb.se/contentassets/ca21efb41fee47d293bbee5bf7be7fb3/weighting-methods.pdf|journal=Journal of Official Statistics|volume=19|issue=2|pages=81–97}}</ref><ref name="battaglia">{{cite journal |last1=Battaglia|first1=Michael|last2=Izrael|first2=David|date=2009|title=Practical Considerations in Raking Survey Data|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/228435832|journal=Survey Practice|volume=2|issue=5|pages=1–10|doi=10.29115/SP-2009-0019|doi-access=free}}</ref>
